claims.claim: The governance checker enforces declared grade arithmetic and byte bindings, with grandfather exemptions. It does not establish that supplied grades or cited evidence prove mathematical correctness.
dependencies: Substantive independent review of grade bases and evidence
limitations: Source omitted from cited run inputs is currently accepted by the freshness check.

file_reviews.assessment: Describes acceptance as byte-bound completed grade records rather than mathematical truth. Explicitly retains baseline exemptions. The claimed run/source freshness requirement is stronger than the missing-input branch actually enforces.

Exact glob populations, runtime L4D/test L2D floors, empty-init pin and byte-based imported baselines. These are declared process categories, not correctness theorems. The new dag audit tools are outside the listed source globs.

Full source: strict Pydantic admission, weakest-gate arithmetic, rational conservative mutation fraction, path/hash binding and baseline exemption. Grades themselves remain assertions. Reproduced _run_problems accepting a cited run that omits the source entirely. Empty evidence lists and arbitrary per-gate text are admitted; therefore evidence sufficiency requires external review.

Full source: argv-only subprocess capture, timeout and start-error records, pre-run governed-source hashes and output hash. Combined stdout+stderr concatenation does not preserve interleaving. Snapshot hashes are taken before execution and do not prove no input changed during the command. Tool results remain recorded evidence, not mathematical proof.
